title: SLO-aware Decision Plane to coordinate regional failback and graceful load admission
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current autoscaler and readiness/liveness checks produce brittle failover behavior in multi-region incidents. When a region degrades, per-service readiness triggers mass drain and the autoscaler thrashes, which causes temporary SLO breaches. We need a lightweight decision layer that centralizes policy about admission, fallback, and circuit state to preserve global SLOs during regional anomalies.

Goal: Design and implement an SLO-aware Decision Plane (SDP) that consumes existing health signals, computes per-route admission decisions (allow/derate/block), coordinates with autoscaler handshakes, and publishes graded circuit states. The SDP should enable graceful load shedding with token-priority support, allow fast regional failback, and minimize autoscaler thrash while keeping tail latency and error-rate SLOs within budget.
impact_summary: Reduces SLO violations during partial-region failures by coordinating admission and autoscaler operations. Expected outcomes: 30-60% fewer transient breaches in P99 latency during regional degradation, reduced autoscaler churn (measured by scale events per hour), and clearer incident runbooks for reroutes and degradation modes.
success_metrics: Reduce P99 generation latency SLO breaches during simulated partial-region outage by >=40%
Decrease autoscaler scale-up/scale-down oscillations during degraded traffic by >=50% (events/hour)
Maintain 95% of high-priority tokens served during graded-degradation tests
Time-to-failback (automated reconvergence after region heal) under 3 minutes in canary scenarios
design_notes: Decision Plane responsibilities: aggregate health signals (readiness/liveness, probe confidence), compute a per-route 'admission score', expose per-region/per-model graded circuit state, and provide an autoscaler handshake endpoint.

Admission scoring: combine weighted signals: probe_confidence (40%), token_priority_pressure (25%), queue_depth_estimate (15%), recent_error_rate (10%), and forecasted capacity headroom from autoscaler (10%). Scores map to: ALLOW, DERATE (percentage), SOFT_BLOCK (reject best-effort tokens), HARD_BLOCK.

Token-aware prioritization: SDP must accept token priority hints from routing layer and support token-weighted admission (route-level budgets). High-priority tokens bypass some derate steps but still respect hard blocks.

Autoscaler handshake: SDP will signal to the autoscaler a 'derate intent' state including target throughput reduction. Autoscaler uses this to avoid aggressive scale-down during transient probe noise. Also SDP can request short-term burst allocations from Dedicated pools when available.

Circuit semantics: circuits are graded (0..100) where >80 implies hard block, 30..80 is derate band, <30 means normal. Circuits include decay periods and require quorum of probe sources to escalate to hard block to avoid single-sensor flip.

Failback strategy: when region health improves, SDP initiates a staged reinjection: warmup percentage increments (5->20->50->100) with short (30s-2m) observation windows and autoscaler hold periods to ensure steady state before removing derates.
Operational signals: SDP emits events to Console: per-route admission score, circuit grade, token-throttled counts, autoscaler handshake events, and canary warmup progress.

Performance constraints: SDP decision latency target <= 5ms in the critical path. Decisions are cached per route/token for short TTLs (200-1000ms) to avoid added latency under high QPS. Fallback: if SDP unreachable, router falls back to local conservative policy (small derate).
implementation_tasks: Design protobuf/gRPC contract for Decision Plane API (GetAdmission(route, token_hint) -> AdmissionDecision)
Implement aggregator service to consume health signals (probe scores, error rates, queue metrics). Include smoothing (Kalman or EWMA) to reduce oscillation.
Admission scoring engine: implement weighted scoring and rule engine to map score to actions. Add config flags to tune weights per route.
Autoscaler integration: implement handshake endpoints and include an opt-in flag for services to participate. Autoscaler change: respect SDP hold periods before scale-down.
Routing layer changes: call SDP in fast path with caching and local fallback. Implement token-priority headers and per-request timeout fallback logic.
Console instrumentation: new dashboards and alerting for SDP metrics and circuit escalations. Add a rollout monitor for staged failback steps.
E2E tests and simulation harness: extend existing chaos harness to simulate partial-region networking faults and probe noise. Include token-priority scenarios and autoscaler noise injection.
Runbook & incident process: write procedures for manual override, emergency unblocking, and rollback of SDP configs.
Security review: ensure SDP endpoints require mTLS and role-based access for configuration changes.
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring engine with edge cases (probe noise, conflicting signals)
Integration tests: routing <-> SDP contract, including local-fallback path
Load test: validate decision latency at 200k RPS equivalent with realistic cache hit ratios
Chaos simulation: partial-region latency amplification, probe flapping, autoscaler slow-convergence
Token-priority acceptance tests: ensure high-priority tokens remain within configured budget during derates
Canary: deploy SDP only for a small percentage of routes/services, monitor circuit changes and SLO impact before larger rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): implement scoring engine and run local sims with synthetic probes. Duration: 2 weeks
Phase 1 (pilot): enable SDP for non-critical internal services, read-only telemetry view for platform team. Duration: 1 week
Phase 2 (limited canary): active enforcement for <5% of live traffic across 2 regions with token-priority tests. Observe for 2 business days
Phase 3 (regional pilot): expand to failover-critical routes in one customer region; enable autoscaler handshake. Observe and tune for 1 week
Phase 4 (gradual ramp): incremental rollout using per-route config until global coverage. Add automatic rollback if SLO regressions detected
Emergency rollback: flip global 'sdp-enforce=false' feature flag and fallback to local router policy.

acceptance_criteria: SDP returns decisions within 5ms for 99th percentile under target load
End-to-end canary demonstrating reduced P99 SLO breaches in simulated partial-region outage
Autoscaler respects SDP hold signals and avoids aggressive scale-downs during derate windows
Operational dashboards show clear circuit transitions and token-throttle counts
Security review completed and playbook for manual override exists
